results.title: Optimizing Images For Web Performance: All You Need To Know | DebugBear
results.snippet: This is especially valuable for logos, icons, and other images that appear on multiple pages. You can control how long browsers cache your images through HTTP headers—longer cache times mean faster repeat visits. Server caching: Your server can store pre-processed versions of your images, so it doesn't have to resize or optimize them from scratch every time someone requests them. This reduces server processing time and speeds up initial page loads.

results.title: Six Tips on How to Optimize Images for Page Speed | Cloudinary
results.snippet: Image optimization can take several forms, ranging from using built-in features like the srcset and sizes attributes of the HTML element, to advanced techniques like image compression and caching. Before diving into optimization, it’s always a good idea to start by checking how your website or app is currently performing. Tools like PageSpeed Insights can help you measure your site’s speed and identify areas that need improvement.
